title: Necrotising Soft-Tissue Infection: Recognition and Emergency Surgical Management
specialty: General Surgery / Infectious Diseases / Emergency Medicine

evidenceAudit.scope: Necrotising Soft-Tissue Infection: Recognition and Emergency Surgical Management
findings: Built as an additive Disease Management version using the approved-topic structure.
Investigations are ordered from bedside/laboratory assessment to imaging and specialist tests.
The original outline remains current; this version is non-current and pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national necrotising-infection antimicrobial schedule was opened.
Drug doses and SFDA registration require local formulary verification.

pathophysiology.summary: Infection spreads rapidly along fascia with thrombosis and tissue necrosis. Toxin production and systemic inflammation cause shock and multiorgan failure. Antibiotics cannot penetrate devitalised tissue reliably; urgent surgical debridement is essential.
keyMechanisms: Infection spreads rapidly along fascia with thrombosis and tissue necrosis.
Toxin production and systemic inflammation cause shock and multiorgan failure.
Antibiotics cannot penetrate devitalised tissue reliably; urgent surgical debridement is essential.

references.title: IDSA Skin and Soft Tissue Infection Guideline

symptoms: Severe pain, rapidly progressive swelling, fever or malaise.
physicalSigns: Pain out of proportion, tense oedema, skin discolouration, bullae, crepitus, anaesthesia or systemic toxicity.
redFlags: Shock, rapidly advancing margins, bullae, skin necrosis, altered consciousness or severe pain out of proportion.
precipitants: Trauma, surgery, diabetes, immunosuppression, peripheral vascular disease or injection exposure.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Superficial inflammation without disproportionate pain or rapid systemic deterioration.
Venous findings without skin necrosis or surgical infection features.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Disproportionate pain, toxicity or tissue necrosis
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Proceed to theatre when suspected; imaging must not delay debridement.

references.title: IDSA Skin and Soft Tissue Infection Guideline

ruleIn.testName: Full blood count, C-reactive protein and metabolic panel
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Inflammation, renal injury, hyponatraemia or metabolic disturbance
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Stage severity but never use a normal result to exclude disease.

references.title: IDSA Skin and Soft Tissue Infection Guideline

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Treat shock and escalate to critical care.
ruleIn.normalValue: Lactate below 2 mmol/L and no acidosis

references.title: IDSA Skin and Soft Tissue Infection Guideline

ruleIn.testName: Blood and deep operative tissue cultures
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Blood cultures before antibiotics if no delay; deep tissue at operation guides narrowing.

references.title: IDSA Skin and Soft Tissue Infection Guideline

ruleOut.testName: Computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Use only if diagnosis is uncertain and imaging will not delay surgery.

clinicalManagement.title: Call surgery and resuscitate
actions: Obtain emergency surgical and anaesthetic review; mark progression and start sepsis resuscitation.
Do not delay exploration for imaging or laboratory scores.

clinicalManagement.title: Source control
actions: Perform urgent radical debridement and plan repeat inspection/debridement.
Send deep tissue for microscopy, culture and histopathology.

clinicalManagement.title: Antimicrobial and critical care
actions: Start broad empirical intravenous therapy covering MRSA, Gram-negative organisms and anaerobes using the Saudi hospital severe-sepsis formulary.
Narrow with microbiology advice after cultures and debridement findings.

medicationPlan.note: IDSA recommends vancomycin or linezolid plus piperacillin-tazobactam or a carbapenem, or ceftriaxone plus metronidazole; documented group A streptococcal disease requires penicillin plus clindamycin. Exact doses are deliberately deferred to the Saudi hospital severe-sepsis formulary, renal function and local resistance data.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: High clinical suspicion is sufficient for immediate surgical exploration; do not wait for a score or imaging.

teaching.scope: Necrotising Soft-Tissue Infection: Recognition and Emergency Surgical Management
learningObjectives: Recognise the emergency and relevant red flags.
Select the correct investigation and escalation pathway.
Use medicines only within the stated branch and local formulary.
pitfalls: Delaying specialist escalation while waiting for a non-essential test.
Using an unverified medicine dose or applying an adult pathway to a child.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval.
keyPoints: Shock, rapidly advancing margins, bullae, skin necrosis, altered consciousness or severe pain out of proportion.

references.title: IDSA Skin and Soft Tissue Infection Guideline

patientEducation: Explain the need for emergency and often repeated surgery.
lifestyleAndDiet: Optimise diabetes, nutrition and wound care during recovery.
mdtReferrals: General surgery, anaesthesia, critical care, infectious diseases, microbiology and reconstructive surgery.
dischargeCriteria: Source controlled, physiologically stable and antimicrobial/wound plan documented.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Surgical wound, rehabilitation and infection follow-up.
